subject: maths
question: In a triangle, if one exterior angle is 120°, and the opposite interior angle is 40°, what is the other interior angle adjacent to it?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Exterior Angle Theorem: Exterior angle = Sum of two non-adjacent interior angles.

Given: Exterior angle = 120° and one opposite interior angle = 40°.

Let the other interior angle be x.

120° = 40° + x ⇒ x = 120° − 40° = 80°.

**∴ The correct answer is 80°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Exterior angle of the triangle = 120°

One opposite interior angle (α) = 40°

**Formula Used:**

Exterior Angle Property: The measure of an exterior angle of a triangle is equal to the sum of the measures of its two interior opposite angles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8207a2f294d70c768666721bb5a21b7122c46ab3daa88417f9cd13b1ab097c39.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Exterior Angle = Interior Angle 1 + Interior Angle 2

⇒ 120° = 40° + x

⇒ x = 120° − 40°

⇒ x = 80°

**∴ The correct answer is 80°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Exterior Angle Theorem

In any triangle, the exterior angle is always greater than either of the opposite interior angles and equals their sum.

Angle Sum Property

The sum of all three interior angles of a triangle is always 180° (Angle A + Angle B + Angle C = 180°).

Linear Pair Axiom

The sum of an interior angle and its adjacent exterior angle is always 180° as they form a straight line.</p
